Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnogram.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apnea.

This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%.
Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, compressing only 10% of total sleep time.

Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Atrial Hypothyroidism (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive
apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with
significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%.
The patient's baseline oxygen saturation was 95%.
No significant periodic limb movements were noted.

A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway
pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to
determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Clinical History: palpable lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. Metogram and ultrasound findings are suspicious for malignancy.

Gross Description:
The specimen is received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and medical record number, and designated "left breast core biopsy". It consists of three tan-white, cylinical tissue fragments, ranging in length from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm and in diameter from 0.2 cm to 0.3 cm. The entire specimen is submitted in one cassette.

Microscopic Description:
Histologic sections reveal cores of breast tissue with an infiltrative neopism. The tumor cells are arranged in irregular nests and hyperlipidemia. The neoplastic cells are pleomorphic with enlarged, hyperlipidemia and persistent nucleari. Mitotic figures are frequently identified. There is associated ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), solid type, with high-grade nuclear features. No evidence of lymphohistochemical invasion is identified in the submitted material.

Diagnosis:
Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Grade 3 of 3.

Comments:
The histopathologic features are those of a high-grade invasive ductal carcinoma. Correlation with imaging findings and clinical presentation is recommended. Further evaluation for hormone receptor status and HER2/neu expression is pending and will be reported in an addendum.

Gross Description:
Received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and "left arm shave biopsy," is a single, circular piece of skin measuring 1.0 cm in diameter and 0.4 cm in thickness. The epidermis is focaly ulcerated and contains a darkly pigmented, raised lesion measuring 0.7 cm in diameter.

Comments:
The features are those of a nodular malignanent melanoma. The deep and peripheral margins are involved by invasive melanoma. Wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy is recommended based on the Breslow depth and presence of ulceration. Clinical correlation is essential.

Biomarkers:
BRAF V600E mutation analysis

Result: Positive
Interpretation: A BRAF V600E mutation was detected in the tumor cells. This finding has therapeutic implications, as patients with BRAF mutated melanoma may benefit from targeted therapy.

Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A).

Patient Name: Jane Doe MRN: 987654321
Date of Birth: 1970-05-15
Accession #: Female
Fax: (123) 438-7890

Date of Collection: 2025-06-16
Specimen Type: Tissue biopsy, left breast
Clinical History: Palpable lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
breathest, Mammmogram and ultrasound findings are suspicious for malignancy.

Gross Description:
The specimen is received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and medical record number, and
designed to left breast core biopsy. It consists of three tan-white, cylindrical tissue fragments,
ranging in length from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm and in diameter from 0.2 cm to 0.3 cm. The entire specimen is
submitted in case.
Microscopic Description:
Histologic sections reveal cores of breast tissue with an infiltrative neoplasia. The tumor cells are
arranged in irregular nests and single files, infiltrating the fibrousstroma. The neoplastic cells are
pleomorphic with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei and prominent nucleoide. Mitotic figures are
frequently identified. There is associated ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), solid type, with high-grade
nuclear features. No evidence of lymphovascular invasion is identified in the submitted material.

Diagnosis:
Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Grade 3 of 3.

Comments: The histomorphologic features are those of a high-grade invasive ductal carcinoma. Correlation with
 imaging findings and clinical presentation is recommended. Further evaluation for hormone receptor
 status and HER2/Neu expression is pending and will be reported in an addendum.

(a) Normal Colon
You have undergone a colonoscopy, a diagnostic procedure in which a flexible, lighted tube was used to examine the lining of your large intestine (colon). The sedation you received for the procedure will continue to affect your judgment and coordination for the rest of the day. For your safety, it is essential that you carefully follow these instructions.

Immediate Post-Procedure Care
Transportation: You must be discharged into the care of a responsible adult who will drive you home. You are not permitted to drive, take a taxi, or ridehare alone, or use public transportation by yourself.
Rest and Supervision: Aresponsible adult must stay with you for the remainder of the day and night. It is important to rest at home for the rest of today. Dietary Guidelines
Begin by drinking clear liquids (such as water, apple juice, ginger ale, or breath) once you are home.
If you tolerate clear liquids well, you may advance to a light meal a few hours later. Good choices include soup, toast, crackers, or yogurt.

Impressions
Normal Colonoscopy: The entire colon, from the cecum to the rectum, was visualized and appeared normal. There were no polyps, masses, diverticula, or evidence of inflammation.
Activity: You may feel tired and bloated for the rest of the day. It is important to rest. Do not drive, operate machinery, or make any important decisions for at least 24 hours. You must have a responsible adult stay with you for the remainder of the day. You may resume normal activities tomorrow.

Diet: You may resume your normal diet as tolerated. Start with clear liquids and light foods (e. soup, gelatin, crackers) and advance to a regular diet if you are not experiencing nausea or significant bloating. Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods for the first 24 hours.

Follow-up: Based on the normal findings of your colonoscopy, your next routine screening colonoscopy is recommended in 10 years. We will send a recheck to you at that time. If you experience a severe abdominal pain, persistent nausea, or vomiting, fever, or significant rectal bleeding, please contact our office immediately or go to the nearest emergency room.

Visit Summary:
This 38-year-old female with a known history of persistent asthma presents with a three-day history of
progressive worsening shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness. She reports developing a
mild upper respiratory infection about one week ago, which has now resolved, but her respiratory
symptoms have since escalated. She has increased the use of her rescue Albuterol inhaler to 6-7 times
per day with only partial, temporary relief. Examination revealed a patient in mild respiratory distress
with a history of osteoarthritis. A DuNeB (lipidopril 10 mg/dL/actuation) and a
lipidopril 10 mg/dL/actuation) nebulizer treatment was administered in the office, which provided significant improvement in her work of breath and
reduced wheezing on succussion. She is discharged with a prescription for a 5-day course of oral
Proninone. The patient was educated on her asthma action plan, the signs of a severe exacerbation
requiring emergency care, and the importance of adherence to her controller medication. She will
follow up with her primary care physician in 3-5 days.

noted.

Hem: Mucous membranes are moist. Mild boggy tissue is noted in the nares. Pharynx is non-
erythematous.

Pulmonary/Chest: Diffuse expiratory wheezes heard throughout all lung fields bilaterally. Good air
entering and expiration is prolonged. No cracks or ronchi. Mild submocostal retraction is observed.

Clinical History: 30-year-old female with an abnormal Pap test result of Low-Grade Squamous
intraepithelial lesion (LISIL) and positive for high-risk HPV.
Diagnosis: Cervix, 6 o'clock, biopsy: High-Grade Squamous intraepithelial lesion (CIN 2).
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled "cervix 6 o'clock", are two fragments of tan-white
mucosal tissue, each measuring approximately 0.3 cm. Submitted entirely in one cassette.
Microscopic Description: Sections show squamous mucosa with marked architectural
disorganization. There is a proliferation of atypical basaloid cells extending into the middle third of the
epithelial thickness. These cells exhibit enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei with irregular contours and a
high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Mitotic figures are noted above the basal layer. The stromal-
eothinial lesion is well-defined.

Comments: The findings are diagnostic of CIN 2, a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion.
Correlation with colposcopy and appropriate clinical management is advised.

Specimen: Cervical biopsy at 6
o'clock
